Contributing to mfrmr

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thanks for helping improve mfrmr.

Before you start

  • Search existing issues and pull requests first.
  • If behavior changes are large, open an issue before implementation.
  • Keep changes focused and reviewable.

Development setup

# from package root
install.packages(c("devtools", "roxygen2", "testthat"))
devtools::document()
devtools::check(args = c("--no-manual"), document = FALSE)

To try a development checkout, start a fresh R session in its package root:

pkgload::load_all(".", export_all = FALSE)
getNamespaceInfo(asNamespace("mfrmr"), "path")

The returned path should identify that checkout. Use a complete checkout or install a complete source archive; copying selected R files can omit internal helpers even when the public function is present. A version number alone does not distinguish development copies with the same package version. If a helper is missing, verify the source files and loaded namespace path before refitting.

Source control and retained evidence

Use a separate Git checkout on each computer, outside file-sync folders. Exchange source changes as commits. A synced .git directory can mix a newer branch reference with an older index or worktree.

Keep maintainer instructions, internal roadmaps and large generated study outputs out of Git. .gitignore does not untrack files already committed, and .Rbuildignore controls the package archive rather than repository visibility. Removing a file from current tracking does not erase it from earlier commits.

Research runners and small synthetic regression fixtures remain versioned. Historical validation records can refer to locally retained output bundles that are not distributed in a fresh checkout. Restore the matching private evidence to its recorded relative paths before replay, preserving source, input and environment identity. Evidence-dependent checks report a skip when these files are absent; that skip is not evidence that the numerical validation passed. Ordinary package tests and hosted checks must not require private roadmaps.

For external programs such as FACETS, transfer a completed input bundle, run it in a local directory, and return a completed output bundle. Record the source commit, program version, settings, stopping status and input/output checksums. Verify the received bundle before comparing results; avoid running against files still being synchronized.

Building from a checkout with retained research results

Stage the package files before building this research-heavy checkout. R CMD build first copies the source tree, following directory links, and only then applies .Rbuildignore. Excluded validation-results/ links can therefore break that initial copy. Do not remove retained research results to fix it.

From the package root:

mfrmr_stage_root=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/mfrmr-source.XXXXXX")
Rscript --vanilla scripts/stage-package.R "$mfrmr_stage_root/mfrmr"
R_BUILD_TAR=internal R CMD build "$mfrmr_stage_root/mfrmr"

The helper prunes excluded directories before traversal, using the running R version’s tools build-ignore rules, and verifies the copied file bytes. It requires a new destination outside the checkout and refuses an existing one. The normal build still applies its remaining exclusions and transformations. This avoids copying research artifacts; it does not skip required package checks, examples or vignette execution.

Inspect build warnings even when the command exits successfully. Before using an archive, verify its expected file list and source contents, then install the archive in a fresh library. Missing-file warnings are a failed build, not a usable candidate. If using an external tar program via R_BUILD_TAR, follow the R build documentation and verify extraction explicitly with utils::untar(..., tar = "internal"); the standalone untar() default may use an external unpacker instead. The internal build method avoids macOS extended-attribute records that the internal installer may reject. An external tar’s successful build or extraction is not sufficient evidence of portability.

Coding guidelines

  • Prefer readable, explicit code over compact but opaque code.
  • Keep public API names descriptive.
  • For user-facing behavior changes, update docs and examples in the same PR.
  • Use base R plotting defaults in this package unless there is a strong reason not to.

Testing expectations

  • Add or update tests for every user-visible change.
  • Keep tests deterministic (fixed seeds, no network calls).
  • Avoid writing plot files during tests (use draw = FALSE unless plotting is under test).
  • Use on.exit(..., add = TRUE) or withr::defer() for cleanup. Replacing exit handlers can discard mock or option restoration and contaminate later tests, even when the test that changed the state passes in isolation.
  • Mock only mfrmr’s own bindings. Import a required dependency function or wrap an optional backend locally, then use local_mocked_bindings(.package = "mfrmr"). Follow testthat’s dependency-mocking guidance and the CRAN namespace policy: do not replace another package’s functions or standard S3 methods. Graphics observers should check the arguments mfrmr sends to the drawing functions; use a positive assertion to ensure the observer actually sees the call.

Documentation expectations

  • Update roxygen comments when function arguments/returns change.
  • Run devtools::document() before committing.
  • Do not pass a partial topic set to roclet_output() in the package directory: its default cleanup deletes other generated help files. Use normal package documentation generation or an isolated output directory for a partial set. A shared topic also needs every contributing source file: isolated output prevents deletion of other topics, but does not preserve omitted method aliases or usages within the generated topic.
  • If workflow changes, update README and/or vignette accordingly.

Use fig.alt for article figures. Reference-example figures receive their descriptions through pkgdown’s documented pkgdown/post-reference.R hook, because pkgdown does not currently offer an example-plot alt-text option. Review the descriptions against the actual figures when changing examples; keep axes, uncertainty and diagnostic limitations accurate. Optional plots must retain the correct description sequence with or without their dependency. The hook preserves existing descriptions and stops on an unrecognized empty example-image description instead of guessing. It runs automatically during pkgdown::build_reference(examples = TRUE) and normal site builds, without changing plot images or adding visible titles or captions.

Run Rscript --vanilla scripts/check-reference-alt.R after changing the hook, then build the affected reference topics with examples enabled. This scoped HTML check does not replace review of the figures or screen-reader testing.

The interactive gallery is a website-only article in vignettes/articles/; its Plotly dependencies are declared in Config/Needs/website. With the matching package installed, run Rscript --vanilla scripts/render-visual-gallery.R from the package root to regenerate the README preview from that article’s code. Then use pkgdown::build_article("articles/visual-gallery") to check the page. Verify labels, interval endpoints and underlying values after conversion, and retain the static figures and tables. A successful HTML build does not replace checking browser interactions and the deployed site’s assets.

Examples and timing policy

The CRAN policy asks for examples lasting a few seconds each and minimal check CPU time. Long tests or vignette calculations may be optional, provided the remaining checks exercise all package features. Keep Rd examples useful and short on slower Windows check hosts; retain substantial analyses in tutorials and the complete test suite. The CRAN Cookbook also documents an Overall checktime NOTE above ten minutes. This is a submission-review criterion, not an automatic ten-minute process timeout.

  • Classify the example’s purpose before changing its workload. Keep a short executable route where it is useful. Put long estimation, simulation and repeated-inference workflows in \dontrun{} with an explicit reason and retain their original data, precision and complete runnable code. For summary(), plot() and other consumers of simulation results, read a packaged synthetic result and execute the consumer. The simulation consumer examples use inst/examples/simulation-*.rds (one result per file); simulation-results.R contains the complete regeneration recipe. Keep settings, warnings and failed runs in the saved object, and explain that a one-replication example illustrates structure, not simulation precision.

  • Ordinary table, plot and report examples reuse fitted inputs and matching diagnostics from inst/examples/*-jml.rds and operational-mml*.rds. inst/examples/ordinary-fits.R gives their complete regeneration recipe. Each example loads its own input, so example() works in a fresh session without a previously executed example or a hidden package-wide fit cache. Label these as saved synthetic analyses; do not load an unused ratings table that appears to drive the analysis. Derive any needed data or labels from that same saved analysis. Keep complete data-to-result code so users can replace the input data; mark lengthy workflows for explicit execution rather than shrinking their data or weakening estimation settings to meet a timing target. The full NOT_CRAN=true suite regenerates the ordinary fitted inputs and compares estimates and diagnostics; ordinary checks verify reuse without refitting. Update the saved inputs when their calculations change.

  • The ordinary test profile retains live RSM/PCM/GPCM (including adaptive integration), two-family GPCM, CML, random-rater and testlet estimation, independent likelihood/gradient checks, anchors, G/D inference, networks and the data-to-report smoke path. More extensive report/plot combinations run with NOT_CRAN=true: calibration and portable scoring remain covered by calibration-public-api, conditional-scoring and gmfrm-portable; anchor precision by anchored-calibration, anchored-facet-intervals and anchored-gpcm; inference/reporting by gpcm-inference-extensions, gmfrm-interval-status, experimental-reporting, report-modules and study-report; FACETS checks by facets-manual-consistency and facets-results. The complete suite retains the larger fixtures and all detailed combinations. Do not shrink fixtures when that changes the numerical or inferential condition being tested.

  • Use example_operational for applied tutorials, example_core for idealized fast checks, and example_bias only when a planted non-null DFF/bias signal is needed.

  • Begin ordinary user examples by loading suitable packaged data. Prefer descriptive object names such as ratings, explain what one row represents, and show which returned table answers the question. Use the packaged G-theory and agreement teaching data for those distinct input structures. Keep manual construction when the construction or a particular edge case is the lesson; do not make simulation code a prerequisite for learning an analysis function.

  • Match the estimator and population assumptions to the example’s question. Do not substitute JML for MML, truncate optimization, or lower integration accuracy solely to shorten a check. Omit diagnostics that do not illustrate the documented function, such as optional residual PCA.

  • Time ordinary examples and any \donttest{} examples. As documented in R Internals, R CMD check --as-cran normally runs examples once without donttest code and again with it. Do not add this wrapper merely to hide expensive code: even the ordinary examples can then run twice. Keep short complete examples unwrapped; retain long workflows in help as explicitly runnable examples and in relevant tutorials. Explain each wrapper. Guard optional Suggests with requireNamespace() or the relevant feature check, rather than relying on \donttest{} to avoid the dependency.

  • Use \dontrun{} for measured long workflows, optional heavyweight integrations and external-software examples. Give the reason and an explicit example("topic", run.dontrun = TRUE) command. This keeps the complete code visible without altering its analysis settings. Writing R Extensions documents this display-only mechanism; brms uses it for its estimation examples. It is not limited to examples that are impossible to run. Reserve @examplesIf interactive() for functions that actually require interaction. Do not hide an error behind a wrapper.

  • For a measured long calculation, a commented recomputation call may accompany an executable example that reads and uses its saved synthetic result. Include the complete regeneration recipe, preserve its data and numerical settings, and check that the saved objects match and replay without refitting. A replay check does not replace numerical tests of the estimator. Prefer a complete \dontrun{} block to commenting out every line of a long workflow. Check optional examples explicitly when their code or dependencies change, reusing matching successful execution logs when only their wrapper changes; do not advertise an unexecuted recipe as a fresh validation.

  • Check that the retained example’s optimization and integration controls support its stated purpose. Show the model’s numerical checks where relevant; no quadrature order is a universally sufficient accuracy setting.

  • Use draw = FALSE in examples that only need to demonstrate returned plot payloads.

  • Do not shrink example data below a meaningful many-facet structure just to satisfy CRAN timing. Reduce what CRAN executes; keep realistic examples in vignettes and in the full packaged NOT_CRAN=true test run.

  • Choose verification from the changed behavior and its callers. Use focused regressions for bounded fixes and reuse unaffected results. Do not repeat the complete test suite for each small fix, documentation edit, or result record.

  • In tests that vary only output transformations, compute an unchanged fit’s joint information or likelihood derivatives once per test. Guard reuse with exact fit and numerical-setting comparisons, and restore bindings afterward. Keep the independent derivative/covariance checks and tests of changed fits, information budgets and integration settings; avoid a suite-wide cache that could conceal stale results. Measure affected files separately from a complete package check.

  • Ordinary checks run the same selected tests in at most two testthat workers, with numerical-library threads limited to one per worker. This follows the CRAN resource limit and testthat’s parallel-test interface. It reduces elapsed time, not the amount of numerical validation or necessarily total CPU time. TESTTHAT_PARALLEL=false retains serial execution; Ncpus / TESTTHAT_CPUS requests are capped at two in ordinary checks. Older testthat versions without the supported interface run serially. NOT_CRAN=true retains the complete regression suite and its existing execution policy. Keep files independent, use session-local temporary files, and verify unchanged test results before accepting a scheduling change.

  • CRAN-time testthat and ordinary push/PR CI run the representative workflow and selected contracts from tests/testthat.R. For broad changes or a batched release review, explicitly enable full_suite when manually running R-CMD-check; only Ubuntu release then uses NOT_CRAN=true. Record the reason and source revision for a full run. Historical full-suite evidence remains tied to its original source and must not be relabelled as a new run. Package checks have no repository-defined time limit; GitHub-hosted runner limits still apply. If an external limit interrupts a run, preserve completed results and rerun only unfinished phases against the same source archive. Do not restart successful numerical tests merely to change a timeout setting.

  • Source-tree-only historical and research validation tests are excluded from the package. Run them only for the affected area, with their recorded source version and optional runtime.

  • Before release, run an --as-cran check with timing enabled and ensure the ordinary and any donttest examples execute. Follow Writing R Extensions: Check timing: set _R_CHECK_TIMINGS_=0, use --timings, and inspect the per-topic mfrmr-Ex.timings file. Record the time spent on static analysis, examples, tests, vignette rebuilding and other check steps; report dependency setup, build and installation separately. Preserve actual skips and unfinished steps. A focused check and the exhaustive NOT_CRAN=true regression job provide different evidence.

  • devtools::check() defaults to env_vars = c(NOT_CRAN = "true"), which runs the full packaged suite. To time the ordinary CRAN selection, set env_vars = c(NOT_CRAN = "false"). This alone does not reproduce win-builder: devtools also defaults to omitting the PDF manual, remote incoming checks and strict Suggests availability. For a staged source archive, use:

    devtools::check_built("mfrmr_0.2.4.tar.gz", cran = TRUE,
  env_vars = c(NOT_CRAN = "false"), args = "--timings",
  manual = TRUE, remote = TRUE, force_suggests = TRUE)

    See the devtools check reference. Record R, OS and dependency versions; local timing is not a Windows result.

  • When reusing executed articles with --no-build-vignettes, retain their build/vignette.rds index as well as inst/doc. Verify that its source, output and extracted R filenames match the current packaged articles; copying the HTML alone does not produce a complete vignette distribution. For byte-identical sources restored by a checkout, retain their matching source timestamps: a newer Rmd timestamp than its reused output raises a check warning. Do not change dates to conceal an actual source change.

  • Packaged teaching data use R’s lazy-data database. Access them through load_mfrmr_data() or mfrmr::dataset_name to reuse loaded objects; data() remains available. Measure data-loading cost before adding another cache. The data guidance recommends comparing compression choices for large databases; smaller files alone do not establish faster loading. Preserve values, attributes and independent user edits when changing the access path.

Pull request checklist

Reporting bugs

Please include:

  • minimal reproducible example,
  • session info (sessionInfo()),
  • expected vs observed behavior,
  • relevant data schema (without sensitive content).
